'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
**[[Afghan peace process]]
***[[President of Afghanistan|Afghanistan President]] [[Ashraf Ghani]] rejects the [[United States]] peace plans, but says that he is open to holding a new [[Elections in Afghanistan|presidential election]] in six months. [https://www.brecorder.com/news/40076924/rejecting-us-peace-plan-ghani-to-offer-election-in-six-months (''Business Recorder'')]
***[[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Afghanistan)|Afghan Foreign Minister]] [[Mohammad Hanif Atmar]] says that [[China]] is working closely with the [[Afghanistan|country]] to restore peace there. He also urges [[India]] to play a role in restoring peace in the country. [https://www.newindianexpress.com/nation/2021/mar/24/hope-india-plays-bigger-role-says-afghan-minister-2280736.html (''The New Indian Express'')] [https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/defence/china-working-closely-with-us-on-peace-process-afghan-foreignminister-mohammed-haneef-atmar/articleshow/81656364.cms (''The Economic Times'')]
***[[United Nations]] special envoy on [[Afghanistan]] [[Deborah Lyons]] says that efforts by the [[United States]] and [[Russia]] should be "focused and coherent" and complement peace talks between the [[Politics of Afghanistan|Afghan government]] and the [[Taliban]]. She also urges an end to the violence in the country. [https://www.reuters.com/article/afghanistan-security-un-idUSL1N2LL1IR (Reuters)] [https://reliefweb.int/report/afghanistan/killings-suffering-afghanistan-s-people-must-end-now-special-representative-tells (ReliefWeb)]
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**A bombing in [[Chaman]], [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]], [[Pakistan]], near [[Afghanistan-Pakistan border|the border]] with [[Afghanistan]], kills three people and injures 13 others. The [[Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan]] has claimed responsibility for the attack. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-pakistan-blast/three-killed-13-injured-in-blast-at-pakistani-afghan-border-idUSKBN2BF2HO (Reuters)]
*[[Naxalite insurgency]]
**At least five security personnel and a driver are killed when [[Naxalite]]s attack their bus with an [[Improvised explosive device|IED]] as it crossed a bridge over a culvert in [[Chhattisgarh]], [[India]]. This is the biggest Naxalite attack of the year so far in the region. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/raipur/chhattisgarh-5-jawans-killed-as-maoists-target-bus-carrying-security-forces-in-bastar/articleshow/81652848.cms (''Times of India'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2020 California wildfires]]
**[[Zogg Fire]]
***Investigations into the 2020 fire that destroyed 56,338 acres in northern [[California]] conclude that the fire began when a [[Pinus sabiniana|gray pine tree]] fell on power lines belonging to the [[Pacific Gas and Electric Company]]. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/us/deadly-blaze-caused-by-pg-26e-power-lines-contacting-pine-tree/ar-BB1eRgzf?ocid=uxbndlbing (Bloomberg via MSN)] [https://www.sfchronicle.com/california-wildfires/article/Deadly-Zogg-Fire-started-when-tree-fell-on-PG-E-16045411.php (''San Francisco Chronicle'')]
*[[2021 Suez Canal obstruction]]:
**The [[Suez Canal]] is blocked in both directions after the [[Panama]]nian-flagged [[container ship]] ''[[Ever Given]]'' runs aground north of [[Egypt]]'s [[Suez Port]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-56505413 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[President of South Korea|President]] [[Moon Jae-in]] receives a dose of the [[Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford-AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] in preparation for a visit to the [[United Kingdom]] to attend the [[G7]] summit in June. [https://thehill.com/policy/international/asia-pacific/544436-south-koreas-moon-gets-astrazeneca-vaccine (''The Hill'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tajikistan]]
****[[Tajikistan]] begins their [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccination]] campaign against [[COVID-19]] on the orders of [[President of Tajikistan|President]] [[Emomali Rahmon]]. [https://akipress.com/news:655902:Tajikistan_starts_vaccination_against_Covid-19/ (AKIPress)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Chancellor of Germany|Chancellor]] [[Angela Merkel]] announces that the [[Germany|country]] imposes an "emergency brake" and extends their nationwide [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] until April 18, which including the closure of shops from April 1 to April 5, amidst a spike of the COVID-19 cases. [https://www.dw.com/en/germany-imposes-strict-lockdown-over-easter/a-56948895 (DW)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Italy]] reports 551 new deaths in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day figure since January, thus bringing the nationwide death toll to 105,879. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/italy-reports-highest-covid-19-deaths-since-january/2185716 (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[President of Russia|President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] receives a dose of a domestically-produced COVID-19 [[vaccine]]; it is unknown which of Russia's current three vaccine candidates was administered. Earlier in the day, the [[Government of Russia|government]] had announced this ambiguity was deliberate, before noting that "all three Russian-made vaccines are absolutely reliable and effective." [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/name-of-vaccine-russias-vladimir-putin-to-take-will-be-a-secret-says-kremlin/ar-BB1eRQzR?ocid=uxbndlbing (Reuters via MSN)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****[[Ukraine]] reports a record 333 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 30,431. [https://www.kyivpost.com/ukraine-politics/covid-19-in-ukraine-11476-new-cases-333-new-deaths-121928-total-vaccinations.html (''Kyiv Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Georgia (U.S. state)]] 
****[[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] reports its first case of the [[Lineage P.1]] variant, which was originally detected in [[Brazil]]. It was found in a resident in [[Newton County, Georgia|Newton County]]. [https://www.13wmaz.com/article/news/health/coronavirus/georgia-covid-variant-brazil/85-560c21f1-51f3-476e-bf09-e945638abbc7 (WMAZ-TV)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***[[Brazil]] reports a record 3,251 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|deaths]] from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 298,843. It is the first time that Brazil has recorded more than 3,000 deaths from COVID-19 in a single day. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210323-brazil-s-24-hour-covid-deaths-surpass-3-000-for-first-time (France 24)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***[[Pfizer]] says that they plan to develop new vaccines for other viruses following the success of their [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|COVID-19 vaccine]] candidate. [https://www.cnbc.com/amp/2021/03/23/pfizer-to-reportedly-develop-new-vaccines-on-its-own-using-mrna-technology.html (CNBC)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2021 Boulder shooting]]
**The suspect in yesterday's [[mass shooting]] at a [[King Soopers]] supermarket in [[Boulder, Colorado]], which resulted in the deaths of ten people, is [[criminal charge|charged]] with ten counts of [[murder (United States law)|murder]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/03/23/us/boulder-colorado-shooting-tuesday/index.html (CNN)]

*[[Child corporal punishment laws]]
**The [[Senate of Colombia]] unanimously votes to approve a bill that prohibits corporal punishment, and any form of violence, as a form of correctional punishment for the upbringing of children and adolescents. [https://www.dw.com/es/proh%C3%ADben-en-colombia-el-castigo-f%C3%ADsico-a-menores-de-edad/a-56974967 (DW)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Israeli legislative election]] 
**[[Israelis]] go to the [[Polling place|polls]] for the fourth time in less than two years. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-56483277 (BBC News)]
*[[Killing of Jamal Khashoggi]]
**[[Agnès Callamard]], [[United Nations special rapporteur|Special Rapporteur]] appointed by the [[United Nations Human Rights Council]], reveals that a senior [[Saudi Arabia]]n official twice threatened to have her "taken care of" if the UN did not obstruct her investigation of the assassination of [[Jamal Khashoggi]]. Khashoggi, who had been critical of the al-Saud dynasty, was murdered and dismembered by Saudi agents in the [[Saudi Arabia–Turkey relations|Saudi Arabian consulate in Istanbul]] in 2018 under what is believed to be the direct orders of Saudi [[Mohammed bin Salman|Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/mar/23/top-saudi-official-issued-death-threat-against-uns-khashoggi-investigator (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2021 Myanmar coup d'état]]
**During a news conference in [[Naypyidaw]], the [[Tatmadaw]] defended the reimposition of the [[Military junta|junta]] and claimed that ousted [[State Counsellor of Myanmar|national leader]] [[Aung San Suu Kyi]] was corrupt, tantamount to [[Graft (politics)|graft]]. No supporting evidence for these allegations was offered outside of the taped testimony of a former colleague of Aung San Suu Kyi, [[Phyo Min Thein]], who has been detained by the military since the coup began. [https://apnews.com/article/aung-san-suu-kyi-myanmar-yangon-f2f63948a58ab67781e1763e1b070c61 (AP)]
